description: Install or update Org Kit config and help entries, copy the org standards and blank questionnaires, write the BMad overrides and check the Atlassian and safe-docx tooling.
args: {-H: headless mode}|{inline values: skip prompts with provided values}
outputs: config.yaml org section, standards_folder baselines, governance_folder questionnaires, _bmad/custom overrides

description: Write cited answers into the Technical Architecture, Data Governance & Privacy and Enterprise AI Risk Assessments (all three unless one is named), plus the organisation's own templates placed in the governance folder, porting answers to similar questions, and list the open questions per lead.
args: {questionnaire: optional, one of TechnicalArchitectureAssessment, DataGovernancePrivacyAssessment, EnterpriseAIRiskAssessment; default all three}|{questions: optional question numbers}
outputs: answered questionnaire .docx and open-question list per lead

description: Walk the Product Lead or Tech Lead through their open questions and record their decisions in the review file.
args: {lead: Product Lead or Tech Lead}|{questionnaire: optional}
outputs: drafts/<Doc>.review.md items with the lead's decisions

description: Draft replies to reviewer comments in a questionnaire and apply lead-approved ones on request.
args: {questionnaire: .docx}|{apply: write approved replies into the document}
outputs: drafts/<Doc>.review.md C-items; threaded replies and tracked changes in the .docx

description: Find new reviewer comments across the governance folder and draft pending replies without applying anything.
Flag approved or applied answers that no longer match the current BMad artifacts and propose corrections.
Record approved answers per project with approver role and date, and retrieve them as reference only.
args: {question: topic or question to look up}

description: Regenerate the token usage ledger from the project's Claude Code logs and say what changed.
Break down what one story or planning phase cost, by step and activity.
Explain what drives the token cost and suggest ranked, concrete savings.
outputs: ranked savings in chat; optional savings.json entries

description: One-line cost summary for a finished story's pull request and Jira comment.

Price the solution from the BMad artifacts (spine, spec, epics) at Azure list prices into an Excel workbook over the build and 3 to 5 years of run: one sheet per environment (monthly, daily, annual), a rate card, delivery team mandays, run support (OPEX) mandays, recurring run costs, revenue, a per-epic view (deliverables, duration, share of the build, API cost) and a multi-year view with net, payback and return on cost; or update an estimate whose artifacts, rates or prices changed.
args: {name: estimate or scenario name}|{update: existing estimate}
outputs: <name>.xlsx, <name>.estimate.json and <name>.infra_cost.csv (infrastructure OPEX daily, weekly, monthly, annual)

description: At the end of the project: how long it took (BMad stages, custom agents, epics), total Claude API calls and their cost at Claude's list prices, added to the estimate workbook as named tables and CSVs for a Power BI dashboard.
outputs: Claude Usage, Claude Prices and Project Timeline sheets; <name>.facts.csv; claude_usage.csv and project_timeline.csv

description: At the end of every epic, the team rates the AI from 1 to 5 and, when it was poor (1 or 2), says what went wrong: coding standard, testing standards, decision-making, not grounded in company data, security / compliance, or other. Asked automatically by the build and the retrospective; kept per epic for the close-out.
args: {epic: optional epic number to rate or re-rate}
outputs: ai-feedback.csv; AI Feedback sheet at close-out

description: Once the epics and sprint plan are done, set a Claude API budget in money for each epic, each sprint and each planning phase still to run, then track actual against budget in the token ledger's final summary and the estimate's Epics, Sprints and Phase Budgets sheets. Offered by epics-and-stories and sprint planning when they finish.
outputs: token-budgets.json; budget columns in token_usage_summary_final.csv; Phase Budgets sheet

description: Keep the employee rate card (day rate per role) that prices the delivery team in every cost estimate.

Before bmad-architecture begins, settle the architecture questions the project's documents leave open (environment, cloud platforms, IaaS/PaaS, Well-Architected pillar ranking, policies, naming, tags, regions and availability, on-premises links, AI, environments, architecture style, migration, security level, approved stack, web, mobile or hybrid, analytics workloads) and the guardrails, confirm a summary, and write them to architecture.md plus one file per cloud provider (azure.md, aws.md ...), which bmad-architecture loads and every AD must honour; or revise them and flag the ADs a change breaks.
Draw a cited C4 context, C4 containers, cloud deployment, data flow or sequence diagram from the architecture spine, challenging its gaps first.
args: {type: c4-context|c4-containers|deployment|data-flow|sequence}|{flow: the named flow for a sequence}

description: Write a cited High-Level Design, or a Low-Level Design for a component, as a Word document from the spine, spec and other BMad artifacts, with its diagrams, open points and a traceability appendix, challenging the gaps first; start from an existing Confluence page or publish the document to Confluence.
args: {type: hld|lld}|{scope: the component an LLD covers}|{confluence: page to start from or publish to}

description: Flag diagrams and design documents older than their architecture spine, name the ADs that changed, and check the spine still honours the architecture principles.
